title: Learning the Past from the Future: Retrospective Reconstruction in Temporal Interaction Networks
abstract: arXiv:2610.33171v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Temporal link prediction uses past interactions to predict future links. In practice, interaction records from web and mobile applications can contain gaps caused by logging failures, API limits or lost records, even when later events remain available. To our knowledge, the extent to which later events help recover interactions within such gaps has not been measured directly for this ranking task. We study retrospective reconstruction using the tgbl-wiki and tgbl-comment datasets. We hide a two-hour window, use its interactions as ground truth, and rank the directed pairs active within it. We compare count-based heuristics and logistic regression models using past information alone or together with 1, 6 or 24 hours of later events. Target pairs and candidate lists remain fixed across conditions, so differences in ranking performance cannot be attributed to changes in candidate selection. translated_title: 从未来学习过去：时间交互网络中的回溯重建
translated_abstract: 时间链接预测利用过去的交互来预测未来的链接。在实践中，来自网页和移动应用的交互记录可能因日志记录故障、API限制或记录丢失而存在缺口，即使后续事件仍然可用。据我们所知，对于这一排序任务，后续事件在多大程度上有助于恢复此类缺口中的交互尚未被直接测量过。我们使用tgbl-wiki和tgbl-comment数据集研究回溯重建问题。我们隐藏一个两小时的时间窗口，将其中的交互作为真实标准，并对该窗口内活跃的有向节点对进行排序。我们比较了基于计数的启发式方法和逻辑回归模型，这些模型或者仅使用过去信息，或者将过去信息与1小时、6小时或24小时的后续事件结合使用。目标节点对和候选列表在各条件下保持固定，因此排序性能的差异不能归因于候选选择的变化。（注：原摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出“回溯重建”新任务，首次直接量化了在时间交互网络中利用未来事件恢复历史交互记录缺口的价值，发现引入后续事件能显著提升对缺失时段内交互的排序性能。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the novel task of retrospective reconstruction, for the first time directly quantifying how much later events help recover missing interactions in temporal interaction networks, showing that incorporating future events substantially improves the ranking of interactions within gaps.
